description:
Evidence (experiments for fz-afu.15, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/afu15y/followup.md, e10.md; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/afu15x/e9.md): with a test-only pop-order knob in Agenda::pop, base json_roundtrip AnalyzeActivation runs are 882 under FIFO and 597 under LIFO (A-out: 815 / 592); base same/2 activations range 8 to 37 over 12 orders (A-out removes that: 8 in all); 00420 DeriveRuntimeDemand evaluations range 645 to 699 over orders. Outputs are identical under every order. So the amount of compile work is a function of the order jobs happen to be popped, and one order does about a third less on json.

Paper first: shrink to the smallest program where FIFO and LIFO differ in runs, answer by hand which runs are necessary, and find the first decision where one order does work the other avoids (e.g. a reader run before its producer's answer is final, then re-run). Fix where that decision starts, so the work follows from facts, not order. Measure: run counts across the 12 orders on the matrix and the distiller should collapse toward one value; no fixture rises. The order knob used for measurement does not ship (or ships only behind cfg(test) as a permutation test, per sorting-is-a-barrier).

Investigated 2026-11-14 (four rounds, scratchpad t93_16/findings.md, probes round3.diff / round4.diff in ../fz-t93-16, uncommitted):
- Mechanism: a recursive return climbs ~10 rungs (p2: val/arr/item, 8 lines); each rung mints new item/arr activations keyed on the unfinished type. Superseded rungs stay claimed and re-run; pop order decides how often (p2 non-final activations 84 FIFO vs 40 LIFO; json 166 vs 16). Outputs and final plan identical in every order.
- They are never retracted because silence reads as unknown: preserved_analysis_claims (non-rebased AnalyzeActivation re-lists prior Activation claims), conclude_preserving_frontier (ActivationInputs grow-only), and the waiting arm recants nothing.
- Refuted cures: E/E2 exact claims (spread narrows, floor rises: each dead rung runs once to withdraw); park unclaimed at pop gate (deadlock: parked rung never withdraws, group never closes); engine retirement by claim count (FIFO p2 stays 123: dead arr/item rungs claim each other in a ring until the climb ends); explicit-unknown per-callsite claims (p2 runs away in 9/12 orders: the grow-only stale rows are what cross ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET and widen the climb, so they are the ladder's termination).
- Conclusion: the order-dependent waste and the climb's termination are one mechanism. The cure is not minting rungs: a climbing return folds to one recursive type. This ticket is the acceptance measure for that step: AnalyzeActivation runs across 12 orders collapse on p2, json_roundtrip, distiller, 00420; outputs identical; no fixture rises. The order knob stays out of production (cfg(test) permutation test at most).
title: Compile work does not depend on the agenda's pop order
